clues.text: This small place is part of the city of Namur. Namur sits in the Wallonia part of Belgium.
clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside Wallonia in Belgium

source.quote: Wépion (French pronunciation: [wepjɔ̃]) is a sub-municipality of the city of Namur located in the province of Namur, Wallonia, Belgium.

clues.text: This place enjoys its own small micro-climate. Sun hits the planted slopes that face toward the west.
clues.narrowing: narrows to a sunny west-slope pocket with its own micro-climate

source.quote: The strawberry has been cultivated there for more than 150 years because Wépion benefits from a micro-climate, sun-exposed plantations on west sloping ground and has a perfect ground for this type of culture.

clues.text: This place stood on its own for many years. In 1977, it joined the city of Namur.
clues.narrowing: narrows to the place that merged into Namur in 1977

source.quote: It was a separate municipality until 1977. On 1 January 1977, it was merged into Namur.

clues.text: Folks call this place the top spot for strawberries in Belgium. They have grown the sweet fruit here for more than 150 years.
clues.narrowing: narrows to Belgium's long-running strawberry capital

source.quote: Located 8 kilometres (5.0 mi) south of the city centre, it is considered as Belgian's strawberry capital, with the Wépion strawberry an established concept in Belgian cuisine. The strawberry has been cultivated there for more than 150 years because Wépion benefits from a micro-climate, sun-exposed plantations on west sloping ground and has a perfect ground for this type of culture.

clues.text: Brewers here turn the famous local fruit into beer. That strawberry beer is a clear sign of this place.
clues.narrowing: confirms the strawberry town that makes strawberry beer

source.quote: It produces a strawberry beer under the brand name La Wépionnaise.

clues.text: This beach resort town is in Spain. It sits on Fuerteventura, one of the Canary Islands.
clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside Spain and its island coasts

source.quote: Costa Calma is a beach holiday resort town in the Canarian island of Fuerteventura, Spain.

clues.text: The usual west winds leave this shore sheltered. Its waters stay protected and calm most of the time.
clues.narrowing: rules out windy, exposed coasts on the island

source.quote: Costa Calma, or the calm coast, got its name from the fact that the prevailing western winds normally leave this part of the coast and its waters protected and calm.

clues.text: This town was developed for tourists in the 1970s. That late start sets it apart from others.
clues.narrowing: rules out older historic towns on the island

source.quote: Costa Calma was developed as a tourist community in the 1970s.

clues.text: Sotavento Beach is near this town. It is a site of note where windsurfers race for titles.
clues.narrowing: rules out island towns without the championship beach nearby

source.quote: A site of interest near Costa Calma is Sotavento Beach, which has been the location of several windsurfing championships.

clues.text: Find the start of the Jandia peninsula in the island south. This resort town sits right there by the sea.
clues.narrowing: confirms the southern peninsula resort town

source.quote: Costa Calma is located in the beginning of the Jandía peninsula in the southern part of the island.

clues.text: This town is in the Free State in South Africa. It lies southwest of the city of Bloemfontein.
clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside South Africa and its Free State

source.quote: Fauresmith is located 130 km south west of Bloemfontein, South Africa. The town, named after Rev Phillip Faure and Sir Harry Smith, is the second oldest town in the Free State.

clues.text: Winters here are extremely cold. The air often drops below freezing in that season here.
clues.narrowing: rules out places with mild winters

source.quote: Winters are extremely cold with temperatures often below freezing.

clues.text: This is the second oldest town in the Free State. Its long history sets it apart from newer towns all around.
clues.narrowing: rules out all but the two oldest Free State towns

source.quote: The town, named after Rev Phillip Faure and Sir Harry Smith, is the second oldest town in the Free State.

clues.text: A railway line runs right down the middle of the main road. Only three towns in the whole world share this odd sight.
clues.narrowing: rules out almost every town in the world

source.quote: Fauresmith is the only town in South Africa, and one of only three in the world, where the railway line runs down the centre of the main road.

clues.text: The National Equestrian Endurance Race comes here each year. Horse and rider teams need three hard days to finish it.
clues.narrowing: confirms the town known for the yearly horse endurance race

source.quote: The town is well known in equestrian circles for the annual National Equestrian Endurance Race, during which the horses and riders must complete a grueling 205 km course during the three days of the event.
